message.content:
The title “best jazz singer” is highly subjective and depends on what you value—vocal technique, emotional depth, influence, or innovation. Below is a list of some of the most celebrated jazz vocalists, each known for a distinct style and lasting impact on the genre. (No single singer can claim an absolute “best” spot, but these names are frequently cited as the most influential and revered.)

| Singer | Notable Contributions / Style | Key Recordings |
|--------|------------------------------|----------------|
| **Billie Holiday** | Pioneered the “talking blues” style, emotive phrasing, and deeply personal lyric interpretation. | *“Strange Fruit”*, *“God Bless the Child”*, *“Lady Sings the Blues”* |
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” she mastered scat singing, impeccable diction, and a pure tone. | *“Ella Fitzgerald Sings the Cole Porter Song Book”*, *“Summertime”*, *“Misty Blue”* |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | Her rich, operatic voice and wide range earned her the nickname “Sassy.” | *“Misty”*, *“Lullaby of Birdland”*, *“The World Is Waiting for Me”* |
| **Nat King Cole** | Smooth baritone, crossover appeal, and pioneering jazz vocal albums. | *“Unforgettable”*, *“Mona Lisa”*, *“The Very Thought of You”* |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | Blends jazz with folk, blues, and world music; known for her husky, expressive voice. | *“Blue Light ‘til Dawn”*, *“The Mirror”*, *“The Blue Room”* |
| **Diana Krall** | Combines jazz standards with contemporary pop, known for her piano skills and sultry voice. | *“The Look of Love”*, *“Live in Paris”*, *“When I Look in Your Eyes”* |
| **Nina Simone** | Though often classified as soul/R&B, her jazz roots and political activism made her iconic. | *“I Put a Spell on You”*, *“Feeling Good”*, *“Sinnerman”* |
| **Tony Bennett** | Classic crooner with a timeless approach to standards and a long career spanning decades. | *“I Left My Heart in San Francisco”*, *“The Best Is Yet to Come”*, *“The Art of the Song”* |
| **Michael Bublé** | Modern crooner who revitalized traditional pop and jazz standards for a new generation. | *“Feeling Good”*, *“Haven’t Met You Yet”*, *“Everything”* |
| **Esperanza Spalding** | Contemporary jazz bassist and vocalist, known for her improvisational skill and genre‑blending. | *“Radio Music”*, *“I Am Not Your Muse”*, *“The Sky Is Mine”* |

### How to Choose the “Best”

1. **Historical Influence** – Billie Holiday, Ella Fitzgerald, and Nat King Cole shaped the early jazz vocal canon.
2. **Technical Mastery** – Ella Fitzgerald’s scat and Sarah Vaughan’s range are often highlighted.
3. **Emotional Depth** – Billie Holiday’s raw vulnerability and Nina Simone’s political conviction stand out.
4. **Modern Innovation** – Cassandra Wilson and Esperanza Spalding push jazz into new territories.

If you’re looking for a definitive “best,” it’s best to explore a few of these artists and see whose voice resonates most with you. Each has left an indelible mark on jazz history.
